Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:12:1.hebrew: הכרזה בב"ד - ואינן נפסלין לעדות עד שיכריזו בב"ד להודיע פסולן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:12:1.english: A proclamation in court - And they are not disqualified from [giving] testimony until they proclaim in court to make known their disqualification.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:13:1.english: Does not require a proclamation - For his transgression is well known to all.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:15:1.hebrew: דבסתמא מכרזינן עליה - אע"פ שלא באו עדים שהכניס עדרו לשדה אחר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:15:1.english: That in an ordinary [case] we proclaim about him - Even though witnesses did not come [to testify] that he brought his flock into another's field.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:17:1.english: A robber by rabbinic law - Those [mentioned] in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:17:2.hebrew: גזלן דאורייתא - החוטף ממש, כגון בניהו בן יהוידע, דכתיב (שמואל ב כג): "ויגזול את החנית מיד המצרי" — הכי מפרש במרובה (ב"ק דף עט:):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:17:2.english: A robber by Torah law - One who literally snatches [property], such as Benaiah son of Jehoiada, as it is written (II Samuel 23): "And he snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand" — this is how it is explained in [the chapter entitled] Merubbah (Bava Kamma 79b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:19:1.hebrew: אוכלי דבר אחר - מקבלי צדקה מן הנכרים, דהוי חילול השם מחמת ממון, והוה ליה כרשע דחמס:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:19:1.english: Those who eat something else - Those who accept charity from gentiles, for it is a desecration of the [Divine] Name for monetary gain, and he is [thus considered] like a wicked person guilty of a monetary transgression.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:1:1.english: Where is your camp? - For you wrote to us: "Shebna and his faction have made peace."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:1:2.english: They backed out on me - They went back on what they had promised me.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:21:1.hebrew: כשר לעדות - דבעינן רשע דחמס, כדכתיב (שמות כג) אל תשת וגו' עד חמס:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:21:1.english: Fit to bear witness - For we require a wicked person of violence, as it is written (Exodus 23): "Do not put [your hand with the wicked to be] a witness of violence."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:21:2.english: Answer me, my Master - Answer me, my master.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:21:3.hebrew: ארבעין בכתפיה - חייב מלקות הוא, אע"פ שאין שם התראה, דאמר מר (קדושין דף פא.): מלקין על לא טובה השמועה, שנאמר: "אל בני כי לא טובה השמועה":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:21:3.english: Forty [lashes] on his shoulders - He is liable to [receive] lashes, even though there was no warning [given], as the Master said (Kiddushin 81a): Lashes are administered for an evil report, as it is stated: “Nay, my sons; for it is no good report” (I Samuel 2:24).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:21:4.english: And [he is] fit? - [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:22:1.hebrew: לאפוקה - לומר: ״מת בעלה״ או ״גירשה״ — דניחא ליה לשוויה פנויה, דתיהוי שכיחא ליה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:22:1.english: To remove her - To say: “Her husband died,” or “He divorced her”; for it is pleasing to him to make her an unmarried woman, so that she will be accessible to him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:22:2.english: To bring her in [into marriage] - To say that so-and-so betrothed her.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:23:1.hebrew: הא עדיפא ליה - דתיהוי אסורה עליה, ולא תיהוי שכיחא ליה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:23:1.english: This is preferable to him - That she be forbidden to him, and not be available to him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:23:2.english: As it is written: “Stolen waters are sweet” - And [therefore] he is lying.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:24:1.hebrew: ניסן - זמן קציר, תשרי — זמן בציר ואסיף:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:24:1.english: Nisan - [The] time of harvest; Tishrei [is the] time of vintage and ingathering.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:24:2.english: Is not called a thief - As [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:25:1.hebrew: באריסא - דטרח בה, ומורה היתירא ליטול דבר מועט יותר על חלקו מפני טרחו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:25:1.english: With regard to a sharecropper - For he toiled in it, and rationalizes taking a small amount beyond his share, on account of his toil.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:25:2.hebrew: ודבר שנגמרה מלאכתו - דמשויה נפשיה כפועל, ומורי בה היתירא, וסבר: לא קפיד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:25:2.english: And an item whose work was completed - For he considers himself like a laborer, and rationalizes [it as] permitted, and thinks: [The owner] does not mind.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:26:1.hebrew: איכר - לאו היינו אריס, ואינו חולק בפירות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:26:1.english: A farmhand - [This] is not a sharecropper, and he does not share in the produce.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:26:2.hebrew: קיבורא דאהיני - כמין אשכול, יש תמרים הרבה בענף אחד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:26:2.english: A cluster of dates - A kind of cluster; there are many dates on a single branch.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:27:2.hebrew: ופסלינהו לעדות - דמשום שכר ממון עוברים על דת, והוו להו כרשע דחמס:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:27:2.english: And disqualified them from bearing witness - For on account of monetary payment they transgress the religious law, and they are [thus] considered like a wicked person [guilty of] a monetary transgression.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:29:1.hebrew: והא משמתינן להו - על הראשונה, וחוזרין ועוברין ושונין בעבירה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:29:1.english: And didn’t we excommunicate them - For the first [offense], yet they go back and transgress, repeating the transgression.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:29:2.hebrew: סברי - האי דשמתינן, משום כפרה הוא על שעברנו, ולא משום דנהדר בן; אלא מותר לחלל יום טוב בשביל המצוה, ונשב בנידוי משום כפרה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:29:2.english: They assumed - This [fact] that they excommunicated us is for atonement for what we transgressed, and not so that we should retract; rather, it is permitted to desecrate the Festival for the sake of the mitzvah, and we shall sit in excommunication for atonement.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:2:1.hebrew: בעל הנאה - כמשמעו, וי"א: משכב זכור:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:2:1.english: A hedonist - According to its plain meaning; and some say: [It refers to] male intercourse.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:2:2.hebrew: סוכנת - מחממתו. וחבירו: "ובוקע עצים יסכן בם" (קהלת י׳:ט׳):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:2:2.english: A companion [sokhenet] - [One who] warms him. And its counterpart is: “And he that cleaves wood shall be warmed by them” (Ecclesiastes 10:9).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:3:1.english: (And it says) “When the foundations are destroyed, etc.” - It is written after [the verse]: “For behold, the wicked bend the bow.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:3:2.hebrew: צדיק מה פעל - הקב"ה, מה שכר שהוא משלם? ולקמן מפרש מאי משמע שתות לשון סיעת צדיקים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:3:2.english: What has the Righteous One done - [That is,] the Holy One, blessed be He — what reward is He paying? And later, [the Gemara] explains what indicates that shatot is an expression for a faction of righteous people.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:3:3.hebrew: אילו בית המקדש חרב - ע"י סנחריב בעצתו של שבנא, "צדיק מה פעל" — איה נפלאותיו של הקב"ה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:3:3.english: If the Temple were destroyed - By Sennacherib through the counsel of Shebna — “what has the Righteous One done?”: Where are the wonders of the Holy One, blessed be He?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:3:4.hebrew: אילו מחשבות של שבנא הרשע אין נהרסות - והכי משמע קרא: "כי השתות יהרסון" — מחשבותיו של אותו רשע הכתוב למעלה, "כי הנה הרשעים ידרכון קשת". ולשון "שתות" — מחשבות, שהוא משית בקירות לבו. "יהרסון" — ראויות הן ליהרס, שאם לא כן, "צדיק מה פעל" — מה פעלו של חזקיהו, והיכא שכרו? "כי השתות" — לשון "ולא שת לבו גם לזאת" (שמות ז׳:כ״ג):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:3:4.english: If the thoughts of Shebna the wicked are not destroyed - And this is what the verse means: “When the foundations are destroyed” — [this refers to] the thoughts of that wicked person who is written of above: “For behold, the wicked bend the bow” (Psalms 11:2). And the word shatot means thoughts, which he sets within the walls of his heart. “Shall be destroyed” — they ought to be destroyed, for if not so, “what has the righteous done?” — what has Hezekiah accomplished, and where is his reward? “For the foundations” [ki hashatot] is an expression [related to]: “Neither did he set [shat] his heart even to this” (Exodus 7:23).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:5:1.english: There was a stone there - Beneath the Ark.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:5:2.hebrew: ושתייה היא נקראת - שממנה נשתת עולם, שנאמר (תהילים נ׳:ב׳): ״דיבר ויקרא ארץ״, ואומר: ״מציון מכלל יופי וגו'״. במסכת יומא (דף נד:) אומר: ״עולם מציון נברא״:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:5:2.english: And it was called shetiyya - For from it the world was founded [nishtat], as it is stated: “[God] spoke and called the earth” (Psalms 50:1), and it says: “Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty...” (Psalms 50:2). In Tractate Yoma (54b) it says: “The world was created from Zion.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:8:1.hebrew: תושיה - על שם שהעולם משותת על התורה ולומדיה, נקראת תושיה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:8:1.english: Tushiyya - Because the world is founded upon the Torah and those who study it, it is called tushiyya.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:8:2.hebrew: מפני השטן - שהוא מקטרג ואמר: תסתפק לעליונים, ולא ימסרו הלוחות ביד משה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:8:2.english: Because of the Satan - For he prosecutes and said: Let it suffice for the celestial beings, and let the Tablets not be delivered into the hand of Moses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:8:3.hebrew: דברים של תוהו - דיבור וקרייה בעלמא, וכל דיבור אין בו גשישה ממש, כתוהו הזה. ואעפ"כ, עולם משותת עליהם. ונוטריקון הוא: תי"ו — תוהו, שייה — משותת:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:8:3.english: Matters of tohu - Mere speech and recitation, and all speech has no tangible substance, like this tohu [formless void]; and nevertheless, the world is founded upon them. And it is a notarikon [an acronym]: tav [is for] tohu; shiyya [is for] meshotat [founded].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:9:1.english: Thought - The anxiety of the heart over a person's sustenance.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:9:2.english: Is effective - It is effective in causing [one] to forget his study.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:9:3.hebrew: מפר מחשבות ערומים - נותן להם מזונות, ומבטל מחשבות מלבם שלא היו מניחין אותן לעשות תושיה. ל"א: מחשבה שאדם מחשב: "כך וכך אעשה, כך וכך תעלה בידי" — מועלת להשבית הדבר, שאין מחשבתו מתקיימת, אפילו לדבר תורה, כגון האומר: "עד יום פלוני אסיים כך וכך מסכתות בגירסא":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:9:3.english: He frustrates the thoughts of the crafty - [God] gives them sustenance and removes [anxious] thoughts from their heart that would not have allowed them to perform tushiyya [i.e., Torah study]. Another explanation: A thought that a person calculates: “I will do such-and-such, [and] such-and-such will succeed in my hand” — is effective in thwarting the matter, so that his thought is not fulfilled, even with regard to a matter of Torah; such as one who says: “By such-and-such a day I will complete such-and-such tractates in study.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:9:4.hebrew: מפר מחשבות ערומים - שאין מחשבותיו עולה בידו, ואפילו לתושיה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:9:4.english: He frustrates the thoughts of the crafty - That his thoughts do not succeed for him, even regarding tushiyyah [Torah].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:11:1.hebrew: הלכה כרבי יהודה - דמכשיר בשיש לו אומנות בלא הוא. וכן הלכה, דמשחק בקוביא לאו אסמכתא היא; ודוקא כשמעות שניהם על הדף, שקורין אישקבי"ר בלע"ז, שהמקום קנוי למי שהרויח לקנות המעות. אבל אותם המשחקים באמנה, אפילו הקנו זה לזה — לא קנה, דאסמכתא גמורה היא ואין קנין מועיל בה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:11:1.english: "The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda" - In that he deems [a gambler] qualified when he has an occupation other than this. And so is the halakha, that playing dice is not an asmachta; and [this applies] specifically when the money of both of them is on the board, which is called eschiquier in the vernacular [Old French for a gaming board], for the place is acquired to whoever wins to acquire the money. But those who play on credit, even if they performed an act of acquisition with one another, [the winner] has not acquired [the winnings], for it is a full-fledged asmachta, and a kinyan is not effective for it.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:19:1.hebrew: אוכלי דבר אחר פסולין להעיד - ליכא לפרושי אוכלי דבר אחר דהיינו אוכלי חזיר, דאי באוכלי חזיר — היכי מפליג בין צינעא לפרהסיא? וכי גרע מאוכל נבלות לתיאבון, דאמרינן לקמן (סנהדרין דף כז.) דפסול לעדות בכל ענין? אלא נראה כפי' הקונטרס, דהיינו מקבלי צדקה מן הנכרים:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:19:1.english: "Those who eat something else are disqualified from testifying" - One cannot explain "those who eat something else" as meaning those who eat pork, for if [it refers to] those who eat pork, how could [the Gemara] distinguish between [doing so in] private and in public? And is it any less [severe] than one who eats carrion out of appetite, of whom we say below (Sanhedrin 27a) that he is disqualified from testifying in all cases? Rather, it appears like the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], namely, that this refers to those who accept charity from gentiles.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:21:1.hebrew: החשוד על העריות כשר לעדות - תימה: מאי שנא מאוכל נבלות לתיאבון, ומפלוני רבעני לרצוני, דפסולין לעדות? וי"ל, דמיירי הכא בחשוד בעלמא, בלא עדים, דאין כאן כי אם שמועה. ומ"מ הא דאמרינן "ארבעים בכתפיה" ניחא, כדאמרינן: מלקין על לא טובה השמועה. אי נמי, הכא משום דיצרו תוקפו, ולא דמי לנבלה, וגם לרביעה, דליכא יצרו תוקפו כל כך כמו בערוה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:21:1.english: "One who is suspected of forbidden sexual relations is fit to bear witness" - [This is] astounding: How is [this] different from one who eats carcasses to satisfy his appetite, and from [one who testifies,] "So-and-so sodomized me with my consent," who are disqualified from bearing witness? And it can be answered that here it is dealing with someone merely suspected without witnesses, where there is nothing here but a rumor. And nevertheless, that which we say, "[He receives] forty on his shoulders," is well understood, as we say: They flog over an evil rumor. Alternatively, here [he remains fit] because his [evil] inclination overpowers him, and it is not comparable to [eating] a carcass, nor even to sodomy, where his inclination does not overpower him as much as with forbidden sexual relations.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:9:1.hebrew: מחשבה מועלת אפילו לדברי תורה - פירש ריב"א: דאגת לב האדם על מזונותיו מהניא לשכח ממנו כל שאר מחשבות, אף מחשבת דברי תורה, שנאמר: "מפר מחשבות ערומים" וגו', וקאי א"נותן מטר על פני ארץ" וגו'. י"מ: "מועלת" — משקרת ולא תצלח. כלומר: אם אדם חושב, הן להעשיר הן גם לדברי תורה, לא יספיק, אלא כשעשה לשמה, כדמסיק:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 26b:9:1.english: "Thought is effective even for words of Torah" - The Riva explained: The anxiety of a person's heart over his sustenance is effective in causing him to forget all other thoughts, even the thought of words of Torah, as it is stated: "He frustrates the thoughts of the crafty..." (Job 5:12) — and [this verse] refers back to: "He who gives rain upon the face of the earth..." (Job 5:10). Some explain: "Mo'elet" [means] it proves false and will not succeed. That is to say: if a person plans, whether to become wealthy or also regarding words of Torah, he will not succeed, unless he acted for its own sake, as [the Gemara] concludes.
